title: Ezekiel 46
paragraphs: ¹ This is what the Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court facing east shall be closed for the six working days, but on the Sabbath it shall be opened, and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened. ² The prince shall enter from outside through the portico of the gateway and stand at the gatepost. The priests shall sacrifice his burnt offering and fellowship offerings. He shall worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate shall not be closed until evening. ³ In the same way, the people of the land shall also worship before the LORD at the entrance of that gateway on the Sabbaths and New Moons. ⁴ The burnt offering the prince brings to the LORD on the Sabbath shall be six lambs without defect and one ram without defect. ⁵ The grain offering shall be one ephah with the ram, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he wishes to give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.

⁶ On the day of the New Moon the offering shall be a young bull without defect, six lambs, and a ram — all without defect. ⁷ He shall provide a grain offering of one ephah with the bull, one ephah with the ram, and as much as he can afford with the lambs, along with a hin of oil for each ephah. ⁸ When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gateway, and he shall leave the same way. ⁹ When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate. No one shall return through the gate by which he entered, but shall leave by the opposite gate. ¹⁰ When the people go in, the prince shall go in with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.

¹¹ At the festivals and appointed feasts the grain offering shall be one ephah with a bull, one ephah with a ram, and as much as the prince wishes with the lambs, along with a hin of oil for each ephah. ¹² Whenever the prince provides a voluntary burnt offering or voluntary fellowship offerings to the LORD, the east gate shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings just as he does on the Sabbath. Then he shall go out, and after he leaves, the gate shall be closed. ¹³ Each morning you shall provide an unblemished one-year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD. ¹⁴ You shall also provide a grain offering each morning — one-sixth of an ephah and one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour. This is a lasting ordinance — a perpetual grain offering to the LORD. ¹⁵ So the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil shall be provided every morning as a regular burnt offering.

¹⁶ This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it belongs to that son. It is his property by inheritance. ¹⁷ But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, the servant may keep it only until the year of freedom; then it reverts to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone. ¹⁸ The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance by forcing them out of their property. He shall give his sons their inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people will be separated from their property." ¹⁹ Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy rooms facing north that belong to the priests. I saw that there was a space at the far western end. ²⁰ He said to me, "This is the place where the priests will boil the guilt offerings and sin offerings, and where they will bake the grain offerings, so they do not have to bring them into the outer court and risk consecrating the people."

²¹ Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court. I saw that in each corner of the outer court there was another enclosed court. ²² Each of these corner courts was forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. All four corner courts were the same size. ²³ Around the inside of each of these courts ran a ledge of stone, with cooking hearths built under the ledge all around. ²⁴ He said to me, "These are the kitchens where the temple servants will cook the sacrifices of the people."
